meta.method: Quantile mapping per lead day (1-7), fitted on the hindcast cache (pipeline/cache/hindcast/: ECMWF IFS 0.25 deg DETERMINISTIC runs from the Open-Meteo Previous Runs API, hourly mm summed to Africa/Lagos calendar days) against IMERG daily totals (events/rain_history_grid_daily.json), pooling all 68 cells: the model's p-th percentile is mapped to the IMERG p-th percentile of the same fit sample (401 percentile points, 0 to 100 by 0.25), and any model value is placed by interpolation. Values above the fit maximum clip to the IMERG fit maximum. In pipeline/forecast.py the mapping is applied to every ensemble member's daily total BEFORE chances, levels, risk windows and the hourly export are computed; each member's hourly values are scaled by that member's same daily factor. The deployed mapping below is refit on all three seasons; every number in validation is leave-one-season-out and therefore out of sample.

fit_period.months: April-November of each season (the hindcast window)

per_cell_adjustment.test: A per-cell adjustment would multiply the pooled mapping by this cell's own tail correction: (cell IMERG p99 + 1) / (cell model p99 + 1), computed separately for each season. It counts as stable only when a cell-lead has at least 5 IMERG >= 40 mm days and a model p99 of at least 10 mm in every season, and its largest and smallest season values differ by less than a factor 1.25.
per_cell_adjustment.conclusion: No per-cell adjustment is used: only 84 of 238 testable cell-leads met the stability limit, because each cell-season holds only a handful of 40 mm days and the per-cell tail correction swings widely between seasons. The deployed mapping pools all cells, per lead day.

validation.design: Leave-one-season-out over 2024-2026: each held-out season is scored with a mapping fitted only on the other seasons. 'Before' is the raw model value, 'after' the calibrated one, both against the same thresholds, so the difference is the calibration alone.

noise.plain: at 40 mm: the calibration newly flagged 5 flood days and lost 0 (exact McNemar p = 0.06); with so few flood days this difference is within noise — treat the improvement as suggestive, not proven.

at 15 mm (the warning threshold): the calibration newly flagged 3 flood days and lost 0 (exact McNemar p = 0.25); with so few flood days this difference is within noise — treat the improvement as suggestive, not proven.

level_rule.rule: A cell-day whose CALIBRATED member-median reaches 15 mm is raised to at least 'medium', whatever the ensemble chances say. The threshold was fixed on the 2024 and 2025 seasons only (each calibrated by a mapping fitted on the other season), as the day-1 threshold with the best true skill statistic TSS = POD - POFD over the candidates 15/20/25/30/35/40 mm; it was frozen before the 2026 test season was looked at. It is 'applied' only when it differs from the 40 mm the chance ladder already uses.
level_rule.criterion: max TSS = POD - POFD at day 1, citywide day-level flags

trust.design: Out of sample, leave-one-season-out over 2024-2026: each season's numbers come from a mapping fitted without it (2024 and 2025 from a mapping fitted on the other of the two, 2026 from one fitted on 2024+2025). The threshold itself was fixed on 2024+2025 before the 2026 numbers were computed.

caveats: The calibration is fitted on one deterministic ECMWF IFS run per lead day (the hindcast), while the live forecast calibrates each of the 51 ensemble members; a single run is noisier than an ensemble median.
Quantile mapping fixes the size of the rain the model does see; it cannot create a storm the model never saw at all.
The reported-flood catalog undercounts real floods, so 'no flood reported' on a flagged day is not proof no flood happened.
With only 19 flood days in the window, every flood-day number here has wide uncertainty; the noise field says plainly when a difference is within it.
